Positive control found with tools/gdl/shapegrep.py lhzu --exact-only: dolphin/gx/GXMisc.c::GXPokeAlphaUpdate (100% matched, REAL Nintendo SDK source). subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: The de-fakematch corpus has been reading the raw *(T*)((u8*)p + K) / offsetof-on-raw idiom as though it selected a different ADDRESSING SHAPE than member access (fused displacement vs indexed x-form, load-with-update vs plain load). Measured directly, that is FALSE for the ordinary case, and the true mechanism is narrower and more actionable. DECISIVE EXPERIMENT (tower.c::playerGiveGargItem, a 35-insn byte-exact function): the raw source `first = (u8*)record + (characterOffset = record->character * sizeof(PlayerCharSave)); if (*(u16*)(first += 8752) & bit) { save = (u8*)record; save += characterOffset; *(u16*)(save + 8754) |= bit; } else { *(u16*)first |= bit; }` was replaced by pure member form `if (record->char_save_ckpt[record->character].boss_attempt1 & bit) { record->char_save_ckpt[record->character].boss_attempt2 |= bit; } else { record->char_save_ckpt[record->character].boss_attempt1 |= bit; }`. The result was NOT a shape change: fndiff reported insns 35/35, opcode multiset IDENTICAL, and the emitted INSTRUCTION ORDER was identical instruction-for-instruction -- including the `mulli r,character,240`, the per-access rematerialized `add rBase,record,prod`, the folded 8752/8754 displacements, the `lhzu` load-with-update, and the `sth r,0(rBase)` store through the updated pointer. The ONLY difference was a register PERMUTATION over the same five registers (target character->r3, const1->r0, bit->r4, prod->r5, base->r6; ours character->r0, const1->r3, bit->r6, prod->r4, base->r5), scoring REGISTER_ONLY real 0 -> 22. Adding ONE named local for the index (`s32 character = record->character;`, member form otherwise unchanged) moved it monotonically toward the target, real 22 -> 18, without changing any opcode or any instruction position. CONCLUSION: what the raw byte-pointer form supplies is not an addressing shape and not a fused immediate -- it is SOURCE-LEVEL VALUE IDENTITY for the intermediate addresses. `characterOffset` and `first` are named locals; MWCC gives a named local's web a different position in its allocation order than the anonymous temporary that the equivalent subexpression of a member chain produces, and that position is what selects the register. The member chain computes the identical values in the identical order, but every intermediate is anonymous. This reframes the whole hazard family: the raw form is an EMULATION OF THE ORIGINAL SOURCE'S LOCAL VARIABLES, not an emulation of untyped addressing. COROLLARY that falsifies the standing folk reading of the lwzu family: `lhzu`/`lwzu`/`lfsu` fusion does NOT require a `p += CONST` pointer-walk idiom in the source. The byte-exact positive control is real Nintendo SDK C in GXMisc.c::GXPokeAlphaUpdate -- `reg = __peReg[1]; SET_REG_FIELD(...); __peReg[1] = reg;` compiles to `lwz r4,__peReg / lhzu r3,2(r4) / ... / sth r0,0(r4)`. Reading and then writing the SAME indexed lvalue is sufficient; MWCC's peephole fuses the second access's address computation into a load-with-update on its own. claim.law.lwzu-idiom-web-retention's prescription to 'convert around, not through' a load-update site should therefore be read as a statement about that law's specific WALKED-LOOP evidence, not as a general prohibition on member form at any load-update site. CONSEQUENCE: classify a failed raw->member conversion by its opcode multiset FIRST. If the multiset is IDENTICAL and instruction order is preserved, the conversion is structurally CORRECT and the residual is a coloring permutation -- do not cycle addressing forms (offsetof vs view cast vs member; claim.law.hazard-base-respell-regression-is-form-independent already shows they land together), and do not conclude the site is 'load-bearing raw'. Instead reintroduce the ORIGINAL's named locals one at a time and watch `real` move monotonically, or route the residual to a WebFrank REGISTER_ONLY rule. If instead the multiset DIFFERS, the ordinary shape laws (multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing, direct-global-member-flips-index-base-association, cached-base-alias-defeats-rematerialized-index-base) apply as written.
